newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ANALYSTS FAVOUR WOLTERS AS OVER ELSEVIER.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS FAVOUR WOLTERS AS OVER ELSEVIER.

text.p: Dutch share analysts were generally more positive about Wolters Kluwer than Reed Elsevier following first-half results from the two business and professional publishers earlier this week.
SNS Securities said in a research note on Friday that it was downgrading Elsevier shares to a Hold from a Buy, saying it saw "little excitement" in the short-term outlook for Reed Elsevier.
SNS analyst Bert Siebrand maintained his Buy rating on Wolters Kluwer, saying it remained a "fundamentally attractive stock with great defensive properties".
ING Barings analyst Andre Moons downgraded Elsevier to a Hold from a Buy but maintained his Buy rating on Wolters Kluwer.

Moons said in a research note he was unimpressed by Reed Elsevier's arguments for disappointing first-half results but that prospects were bright for Wolters Kluwer and its shares were modestly valued within the publishing sector.
Bas Nienhaus at Effectenbank Stroeve maintained Long-Term Investment ratings for both Wolters Kluwer and Elsevier but said he had a preference for Wolters based on current prospects.

Jeff Meys at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said the average growth of 8.2 percent which he expects in Reed Elsevier's earnings before interest, tax and depreciation over the next four years was already more than discounted by the current share price.
He said he saw limited upside potential for Elsevier shares and rated them a Hold.
Generale Bank Oyens & Van Eeghen lowered its short-term rating for Elsevier to Hold from Buy but maintained its long-term Buy rating.
